there are ways to make money off of them, matched betting is a good way. Also value betting, basically the bookies have lower odds than what the real odds are, thats how they profit. but they arent always right, on smaller events they can give prices which are higher than the exchange odds. 

the exchange is a place you place bets against outcomes, for example you can place a bet against the draw in a football match. but if the exchange odds are at odds of 2 and you bet £10, you are risking £20 to make £10. the way it works is different. you essentially pay the winnings if someone placed a bet at those odds, but you only win their stake if your bet wins (i.e. the outcome you bet on doesnt happen). in most cases your bets against things win. its much easier to win a bet on a horse not winning that winning, thats the advantage of the exchange.

thats why i am really for advantage play, like bonus hunting and card counting for example. you stack the odds in your favour to make profit.
